rationale:
Round 2 at 0783a507. Two duties: (1) classify my round-1 ask, (2) security-screen the NEW G1 attestation code for unguarded operands.

(1) MY ROUND-1 ASK: ADDRESSED, verified by direct source read. internal/gitutil/materialize.go:356-374 ClearMaterializationMarker now calls rejectOptionLike on BOTH the composed ref and expectedOID before building the update-ref -d argv, exactly my preferred fix (adding the missing runtime gate rather than just reclassifying the table entry). The argv-audit-table note (internal/lint/ratchet_argv_table_test.go:136) was rewritten to match: it now states the gate exists, names the R12/G8 commit, and explicitly narrates that the OLD note's claim was false and is now true -- a self-correcting artifact-integrity fix I have no further ask on.

(2) G1 ATTESTATION OPERAND-LEVEL AUDIT: recordStageMarkerAttestation/readStageMarkerAttestation (internal/complete/materialize.go:101-134) route through bead.MergeMetadata/GetMetadata, both of which idvalidate.BeadID-gate issueID before any bd spawn (internal/bead/bdcli.go:322-357,417+), and MergeMetadata's --metadata value is json.Marshal'd into ONE argv token (no shell, no injection surface there). The oid value written is always a git-computed hex SHA from this file's own RevParseRef/marker-publish chain, never free text. At the narrow argv-injection level this code is clean -- no unguarded operand.

But I went further than the operand-gating question and EXECUTED an adversarial check on the mechanism itself (ADR-0042's whole point is consumer-boundary soundness, not just argv escaping), and it reveals a MAJOR gap that defeats the entire purpose of the G1 fix. I built a real scratch bd project (bd init; real dolt backend, bd v1.1.0) and proved empirically: `bd update <id> --metadata '{"mindspec_stage_marker_oid":"<any-sha-i-choose>"}'` is an ORDINARY, unauthenticated bd subcommand -- I ran it against an arbitrary bead and immediately read the exact value back via `bd show --json`. There is NO technical distinction between mindspec's own recordStageMarkerAttestation call and an adversary calling the identical bd command directly: both are literally the same CLI invocation, with the identical key, against the identical unrestricted metadata store.

ADR-0041's amendment frames the threat this closes as 'the ref and the trailer are both authorable with ordinary repo git access' -- true, and R6's round-1 repro proved it. But the fix's OWN security property rests entirely on an UNSTATED assumption: that the same adversary who has ordinary git-commit access in a bead worktree does NOT also have ordinary bd CLI access. That assumption is false in every realistic mindspec deployment this project's own docs describe: bd is mandatory, on-PATH tooling for the SAME implementer agent's own legitimate workflow (claim/close/update its own bead) per CLAUDE.md's 'Beads Issue Tracker' section and AGENTS.md -- there is no scenario where an agent can `git commit` in its own bead worktree but cannot also `bd update` its own bead's metadata. Concretely, the full R6-style attack (verified by re-deriving leg xxiv's exact setup, then adding one line): author the same hand-crafted commit with a clean Mindspec-Stage trailer + smuggled content (leg xxiv's own forgedTip), `git update-ref refs/mindspec/materialized/<bead> <forgedTip>` (leg xxiv's own step), and now ALSO `bd update <bead> --metadata '{"mindspec_stage_marker_oid":"<forgedTip>"}'` -- a single extra, completely ordinary CLI call the adversary already has every capability to make. resolveMaterializationDiscriminator's attestedOrClear() (materialize.go:218-230) does nothing more than `attested == oid`: no nonce, no timestamp, no session/process binding, no signature -- just a string compare against a value the same actor who forged the ref can trivially set to match. tip==oid, attested==oid ⇒ foreign=false ⇒ the discriminator returns the (attacker-chosen) stage as a genuine resume, and per this file's own documented contract ('Run's own resumeStage guard means the panel gate is likewise never re-run on a resume') the panel gate, the content gates, and the re-snapshot are ALL skipped -- the identical catastrophic bypass R6 executed in round 1, reopened by a one-line addition to the exact same forgery. This is EVIDENCE-BEARING (I produced the proof, not an argument), which is why I am marking hard_block: the round-1 MAJOR this commit was supposed to close is not closed against the threat model the round-1 consolidation itself already established (an agent with ordinary repo access) -- it is closed only against a narrower, unstated, and unrealistic sub-case of that same adversary (one who can forge git objects but is somehow presumed to lack the SAME tool the mindspec binary itself uses one line later in the same call graph).

Why this is a design problem, not a one-line patch: git refs, git commit trailers/content, AND bd metadata are ALL agent-writable in this project's own established threat model (ADR-0042 SS1's 'no id operand trusted by provenance' finding generalizes past ids to every store this spec's own G1 amendment relies on). Any 'evidence' stored in a place the SAME actor performing the forgery can also write provides no real separation. The one capability plane this codebase already has that is NOT symmetric with the implementer agent's normal toolset is commit SIGNING with an operator-held key: MaterializeStageCommit (gitutil/materialize.go:200-226) already signs the marker commit when CommitSigningEnabled is on, via the `-S` git flag -- but the discriminator never verifies that signature; it only reads the trailer text and (now) an equally-forgeable metadata flag. Verifying the marker commit's signature against a key the operator's environment controls (not exposed to the implementer agent's normal credential surface) is a genuinely different capability plane and the most promising fix already half-built in this file. The weaker but honest alternative is to explicitly document this as an ACCEPTED residual of the insider/agent threat model (parallel to ADR-0042 SS4's named TOCTOU residual) rather than presenting G1 as closing R6's finding when it narrows the forgery surface without closing it.
concrete_changes_required: Either (a) close the gap for real: make the discriminator's resume-authorization depend on a capability the implementer agent does not normally hold -- the most direct path already exists in this file's own signing support (gitutil.MaterializeStageCommit's CommitSigningEnabled/-S). When signing is enabled, verify the marker commit's signature against an operator-trusted key before honoring ANY resume (attestedOrClear becomes signature-verified-AND-attested, not attested alone); when signing is disabled, the resume-skip-the-panel-gate optimization should be explicitly documented as trusting the local operator's environment, not as closing R6's adversarial finding. OR (b) if a full signature-based fix is out of scope for this round, at minimum rewrite ADR-0041's amendment and materialize.go's doc comments to state plainly that the bd-metadata attestation narrows the round-1 forgery (raises the ref-and-trailer-only bar by one ordinary bd call) but does NOT close it against an actor who also has bd CLI access -- which, per this project's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, is every implementer agent by design -- and file a tracked follow-up bead for the signature-verification escalation, citing its ID in the fix report. Do not let the round-2 consolidation describe G1 as 'ADDRESSED'/closed without one of these two dispositions; the empirical proof in this verdict (a real bd init + `bd update --metadata` round-trip, and the one-line addition to leg xxiv's own forgery) is the falsifiable basis -- re-derive it before disputing.

findings.title: The G1 write-ahead-marker attestation is forgeable by the same actor R6's repro already assumes, via one ordinary `bd update --metadata` call — the panel-gate bypass is reopened, not closed
findings.detail: Empirically verified: `bd update <id> --metadata '{"mindspec_stage_marker_oid":"<attacker-chosen-value>"}'` is an unauthenticated, ordinary bd subcommand (proved with a fresh `bd init` scratch project — real dolt backend — then a round-trip write+read of the exact key). recordStageMarkerAttestation (internal/complete/materialize.go:124-134) writes through this identical, unrestricted call. resolveMaterializationDiscriminator's attestedOrClear (materialize.go:218-230) authorizes a resume on nothing more than `attested == oid` — a plain string compare, no nonce/timestamp/signature. An adversary who can author the hand-crafted commit + `git update-ref` forgery R6's round-1 repro already executed (leg xxiv, bead6_fixture_legs_test.go:1660) can, with one additional ordinary bd call using the SAME bd binary the implementer agent already needs for its own bead lifecycle, set the attestation to match their forged marker OID exactly — reopening the identical bypass (panel gate, content gates, and the re-snapshot all skipped) that G1 was written to close. The unstated assumption that git-commit-capable and bd-metadata-capable are separate adversary capabilities does not hold in this project's own deployment model (bd is mandatory on-PATH tooling for the same implementer agent, per CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md).
findings.location: internal/complete/materialize.go:101-134 (recordStageMarkerAttestation/readStageMarkerAttestation), :218-230 (attestedOrClear), :232-273 (both resume legs); internal/bead/bdcli.go:322-357 (MergeMetadata); .mindspec/adr/ADR-0041-gate-before-mutate.md:397-412 (the provenance amendment whose threat-closure claim this finding falsifies)
